name: Cooking from your stock
desc: Meals from your emergency food: no-cook breakfasts and salads, one-pot meals on a camping stove, saving gas and water, flatbread

guides.t: Meals from your stock without cooking
guides.w: No power, no gas: still a proper meal
s: Every meal: something filling (crackers, beschuit, muesli) + protein (fish, meat, beans, nuts) + fruit or vegetables (tins, dried fruit).
Breakfast: muesli or oats soaked in UHT milk, with raisins. Or crackers with peanut butter and jam.
Lunch: crackers with tuna or sardines, and a tin of fruit in juice.
Dinner: a cold salad from tins (see the tuna and bean salad), with crackers.
Snacks for energy: nuts, a muesli bar, chocolate, dried apricots.
Drink enough: at least 2 litres of water a day, more when it's warm. Juice and UHT milk count too.
Open only what you'll eat now. Leftovers from an opened tin: cover them, keep them cool and eat them the same day.
d: Don't eat from bulging, leaking or badly dented tins
Without a fridge, nothing opened keeps until tomorrow

s: Open 1 tin of tuna, 1 tin of white beans or chickpeas, and 1 tin of sweetcorn or peas.
Drain the beans and vegetables. Keep the liquid: you can use it in soup later.
Mix everything in a bowl with the tuna, including its oil.
Season with salt, pepper and, if you have them, dried herbs, a splash of vinegar or lemon juice.
Eat it with crackers or crispbread. Tinned mackerel, chicken or extra beans work just as well.

guides.w: A warm-feeling breakfast without a stove
s: Per person: 50 g oats or muesli (about 5 tablespoons) and 150 ml UHT milk or water.
Stir it in a cup or jar and add a handful of raisins or chopped dried apricots.
Leave it covered for at least 2 hours, or overnight in a cool place.
Stir again and add honey, jam, nuts or tinned fruit. Eat it the same morning.

guides.t: Cooking on a camping stove safely
guides.w: Gas or spirit stove when the power is out
s: Cook outside, or in a room with a window wide open. Never in a closed room or a tent, and never to heat the room.
Put the stove on a flat, stable surface that can't burn, away from curtains and things that catch fire.
Use a small pan with a lid: it boils faster and uses half the gas.
Stay with it while it burns, and keep children and pets away.
Change gas cartridges outside, with the stove cold and no flames nearby.
Have a lid or a damp tea towel ready to smother a pan fire. Never water on burning fat.
d: Never use a barbecue or camping stove indoors: carbon monoxide has no smell and can kill

guides.t: Saving gas and water when you cook
guides.w: Make your stock and your gas last
s: Lid on, always. Turn the flame down as soon as it boils: a gentle simmer cooks just as well.
Soak pasta, rice or lentils in cold water for an hour first: they then cook in a few minutes.
Cook in just enough water that it's all absorbed (rice: twice its volume), so no water is poured away.
Use the liquid from tins of vegetables and beans as cooking water or for soup.
Hay-box cooking: bring it to the boil for 2 minutes, then wrap the pan in towels, a blanket or a sleeping bag. Rice is done in 30–40 minutes, lentils in an hour, without gas.
Cook once a day for everyone, and eat the rest cold.
d: Food in a hay-box must stay hot: eat it within 2 hours

guides.t: One-pot rice with vegetables and meat
guides.w: A hot meal with one pan, for 2
s: Put 150 g rice (about 1 cup) and 300 ml water (2 cups) in a pan with a pinch of salt.
Bring it to the boil, put the lid on, turn the flame as low as it goes and cook for 12–15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Drain 1 tin of vegetables (peas and carrots, sweetcorn or beans) and 1 tin of meat, chicken or fish.
Stir them into the rice for the last 3 minutes, just to heat through.
Season with soy sauce, stock powder, curry powder or dried herbs if you have them.
Short of gas? Do the last 10 minutes as a hay-box (see Saving gas and water).

guides.t: One-pan pasta with tomato and tuna
guides.w: Pasta without pouring away water, for 2
s: In one pan: 1 tin of chopped tomatoes, the same tin filled with water, a splash of oil and a pinch of salt.
Bring it to the boil and add 180 g pasta (small shapes cook fastest).
Simmer with the lid half on, stirring now and then, for about 12 minutes, until the pasta is soft and the sauce has thickened. Add a little water if it gets dry.
Stir in a drained tin of tuna, or beans for a vegetarian version, and heat 1 minute.
Season with dried herbs, pepper or a little sugar if the tomatoes are sour.

guides.t: Bean and vegetable soup from tins
s: Empty a tin of soup or tomatoes, a tin of beans or lentils (with their liquid) and a tin of vegetables into a pan.
Add a cup of water or the liquid from other tins, and a stock cube if you have one.
Heat it until it bubbles, stirring now and then: about 5 minutes.
Mash some of the beans with a fork to make it thicker.
Eat it with crackers, beschuit or hard bread broken into the soup.

guides.w: Fresh bread from flour, water and salt
s: Mix 150 g flour, a pinch of salt, 1 tablespoon of oil and about 100 ml water into a soft dough. Knead it for 2 minutes.
Divide it into 4 balls and press or roll them flat, about 3 mm thick.
Heat a dry frying pan on a medium flame.
Bake each flatbread 1–2 minutes per side, until it puffs up and gets brown spots.
Keep them wrapped in a cloth so they stay soft. Eat them with soup, beans or peanut butter.
Per 2 people: 75 g rice (short-grain if you have it), 500 ml UHT milk and 2 tablespoons of sugar.
Bring the milk and rice to a gentle boil in a pan with a lid, stirring so it doesn't stick.
Simmer on the lowest flame for 25–30 minutes, stirring now and then, or use the hay-box for an hour.
It's ready when the rice is soft and it's thick and creamy. Add raisins, cinnamon, jam or tinned fruit.
d: Milk burns easily: keep the flame low and stir
